title: Perf canary: on-call runbook + escalation matrix (runtime / infra / telemetry)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Create the production on-call runbook for perf-canary alerts and define clear escalation paths between Serving Runtime (kernel + scheduling), Infra/Fleet, and Telemetry/Observability. The goal is to reduce time-to-triage and avoid ping-pong during active incidents.

Deliverables:
- Confluence runbook with step-by-step validation + decision tree.
- Escalation matrix with owners, paging targets, response expectations, and handoff criteria.
- Ensure alert payloads include runbook + dashboard links (coordinate with incident-bot + observability-pack).
acceptance_criteria: Runbook is published in Confluence and linked from warning + paging alert definitions
Alert payload includes: model, region, baseline ref, observed delta, confidence/min-samples, dashboard link, trace/log links
Escalation matrix names primary and secondary responders per suspected cause (kernel/scheduler vs infra/fleet vs telemetry pipeline)
Runbook includes safe mitigations (rollback/disable switch/QPS cap) with explicit guardrails and approval expectations
SRE sign-off for paging hygiene prior to enabling paging in phase-1 region
implementation_notes:
Notes to incorporate from earlier rollout:
- Avoid false positives due to baseline drift and label cardinality; include a 'telemetry sanity check' section before treating as real regression.
- Ensure runbook distinguishes between end-to-end latency regressions vs runtime-only regressions vs queueing-only regressions.
- Include a standard triage template for incident Slack threads so responders capture required context for postmortems (runtime build tag, kernel tag, fleet SKU, baseline version id, config commit/audit id).
runbook_outline_draft:
RUNBOOK: Perf Canary Regression Alert (prod)

0) Quick context (what is perf-canary?)
- Always-on synthetic workload per model (+ optional region/SKU) to detect p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops.
- Canary does NOT use customer prompts. Canary uses a fixed prompt-shape distribution.

1) Confirm the alert is actionable (anti-flap / telemetry sanity)
A. Check alert fields
- Model (canonical): <model_id>@<model_version>
- Region / tier / sku (if present)
- Regression type: p95_e2e_ms, p95_runtime_ms, tokens_per_sec, queueing_ms, prefill_ms, decode_ms
- Observed delta vs baseline and min-samples met

B. Telemetry pipeline sanity checks (common false-positive class)
- Grafana panel: 'perf-canary metric ingestion delay' (if available) or compare dashboard timestamps vs wall clock.
- Confirm metrics are present for BOTH 'canary' and 'prod_traffic' (if panel exists) to rule out missing-series artifacts.
- If missing/late: treat as telemetry issue; escalate to Telemetry (see matrix) and mute alert with reason.

2) Validate regression is real
A. Compare against baseline
- Open dashboard: Perf Canary → Per-model Overview → select model + region
- Confirm sustained regression: > N minutes and sample count > min_samples
- Compare p50/p95/p99; look for tail-only regressions (p50 stable, p95/p99 up)

B. Determine where time increased (attribution)
- If runtime-only latency increased but queueing stable → likely kernel/runtime/model-config
- If queueing time increased (queueing_ms up, batch size distribution shifts) → likely scheduler/capacity/fleet
- If tokens/sec dropped but latency flat → batching or kernel selection change; also check GPU clocks/thermal/fleet

3) Triage decision tree (first 15 minutes)
A. Is the regression isolated?
- Single region/SKU only → suspect fleet change, GPU pool saturation, regional incident, capacity tier config
- All regions for a model → suspect model config change, runtime release, kernel selection change
- Many models in a region → suspect fleet/hardware or scheduler change

B. Recent changes to correlate
- Runtime build tag / release version
- Kernel selection id / kernel version tags
- Scheduler config changes (batching heuristics, queue limits)
- Fleet changes (GPU driver, firmware, SKU mix, autoscaler)
- Canary config changes (prompt shapes, QPS, model list)

4) Mitigation options (ordered by safety)
A. If alert noise / telemetry issue
- Temporarily silence canary alert rule for affected series (per policy) and open ticket to Telemetry
- Do NOT roll back runtime if telemetry is suspect

B. If real regression but low blast radius
- Reduce canary QPS (to preserve customer capacity) if canary overhead contributes
- Pin kernel selection to last-known-good (if feature flag exists) for affected model/SKU
- Roll back last model config update (if the model registry pushed a config-only change)

C. If sustained regression on top model (paging)
- Initiate rollback of runtime release in affected region(s) per release runbook
- Consider temporary rollout freeze if regression coincides with active deploy train

D. Emergency safety switch
- Disable perf-canary in a region only if it is contributing to incident load or interfering with inference endpoints (should be rare; requires SRE approval in incident thread).

5) Escalation and ownership (see matrix)
- Identify likely primary owner by metric signature.
- Page/notify only per severity policy; avoid mass paging.

6) Documentation during incident
- In incident Slack thread, paste:
  - Model + version
  - Region + SKU + tier
  - Baseline id + baseline window
  - Observed delta + min-samples
  - Runtime build tag + kernel tag
  - Recent deploys (runtime, fleet, scheduler config, model config)
  - Actions taken

7) Exit criteria
- Metrics return to baseline band and remain stable for 2 evaluation windows
- Alert deduped/closed in incident-bot
- If rollback: confirm post-rollback baseline alignment and note in release channel

8) Follow-up
- File root-cause ticket with owner team
- If false positive: add to noise backlog (ENG-4882) with specific series + reason
escalation_matrix:
ESCALATION MATRIX (perf-canary)

Severity definitions (source: SRE policy)
- Warning: regression beyond threshold but limited duration or not top-model; notify #eng-runtime; no page.
- Paging (Sev2): sustained regression on top model OR multi-model regression in a region; page on-call.
- Paging (Sev1): widespread/critical (multiple top models, multi-region) with customer impact indicators; page runtime + SRE lead; consider incident commander.

Primary responders by signature
1) Likely Kernel-level regression
- Signal: runtime-only latency up, tokens/sec down, stable queueing; correlates to kernel tag changes
- Notify: #eng-runtime
- Escalate/Page: Kernel lead on-call (Hiro Tanaka) via runtime on-call
- Handoff criteria: confirmed kernel tag change or kernel auto-selection shifted

2) Likely Scheduler / batching regression
- Signal: queueing_ms up, batch size distribution shifts, p95 tail increases, tokens/sec may drop
- Notify: #eng-runtime
- Escalate: Scheduling lead (Sofia Ivanova) via runtime on-call
- Handoff criteria: queueing is dominant contributor or scheduler config deploy identified

3) Likely Fleet / Infra regression (regional)
- Signal: single region/SKU affected across many models; GPU utilization anomalies; clocks/driver updates; capacity saturation
- Notify: #eng-infra + #eng-sre
- Escalate/Page: Fleet/Infra on-call (Vanessa Ortiz is escalation contact; page via SRE on-call)
- Handoff criteria: multiple models impacted in same region/SKU or recent fleet change confirmed

4) Likely Telemetry / Observability issue
- Signal: missing series, ingestion lag, sudden step changes aligned with schema change, baseline fetch errors
- Notify: #eng-platform
- Escalate: Telemetry platform lead (Logan Wright) and Metrics/Baselines (Nadia Rahman)
- Handoff criteria: ingestion delay > alert window OR label-cardinality drop/shift OR baseline store errors

5) Likely Model registry / versioning issue
- Signal: regression starts exactly at model version/config change; only one model impacted across regions
- Notify: #eng-runtime + model registry partner
- Escalate: Quentin Harris
- Handoff criteria: config-only rollout or version alias change detected

Paging + response expectations
- First response: SRE on-call acknowledges page in <5 min.
- Triage owner assignment in <10 min (Runtime vs Infra vs Telemetry).
- If not acknowledged by owner team in 10 min, SRE escalates to secondary contact.

Slack channels
- Runtime: #eng-runtime
- SRE/on-call: #eng-oncall, #eng-sre
- Telemetry/observability: #eng-platform
- Releases: #eng-releases
- Incidents: #incidents (incident-bot thread)

Key links to include in every alert
- Grafana: Perf Canary → Per-model Overview (with model + region pre-selected)
- Runbook: Confluence runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert
- Release notes: latest runtime release changelog
- Canary config audit: control-plane config change log (model list + thresholds)

Anti-ping-pong rule
- Only one team owns the incident at a time (declared in incident thread).
- Transfers must include: hypothesis, evidence (panels/metrics), and explicit ask.

2026-01-22 (Sean Gallagher): Looks good. Please add an explicit 'telemetry sanity check' section up front; we’ve had alerts where ingestion lag made it look like a step regression. Also clarify when it’s acceptable to disable canary (should be rare, requires SRE approval).

2026-01-24 (Allison Grant): Please align severity language with SLO toolkit (warning vs page, Sev2 vs Sev1). Also ensure alert payload requirement includes direct dashboard link with variables pre-filled (model, region, sku).

2026-01-27 (Noah Patel): Added runtime attribution heuristics to the runbook: queueing_ms dominance => scheduler/capacity; runtime_ms dominance => kernel/model-config. Also added required context to capture: runtime build tag + kernel tag + model version.

2026-02-03 (Logan Wright): Telemetry section is accurate. Added note: if baseline fetch errors appear, treat as telemetry/config-store issue first. Please link to the baseline artifact location and the 'ingestion delay' panel once merged to the dashboard.

2026-02-07 (Rafael Mendes): Runbook published and linked from observability-pack alert rules PRs. Added anti-ping-pong rule + transfer checklist. Waiting for final SRE sign-off on paging hygiene wording.

2026-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): Approved. This is sufficient for phase-1 paging. Follow-up: after first week of paging, capture feedback and update the runbook with real incident examples (file under ENG-4882 noise reduction backlog).
